_note: Families are the top level of the library: ten areas a person looks in (UI, prompting, security...). Every cluster belongs to one family, and a bundle to the family most of its skills are in (its purpose decides a tie). `categories` places the clusters that have no rule of their own ('other-<category>'). Order is the order shown.

families.name: Design and UI
families.blurb: Interfaces that look and feel right: components, styles, motion, accessibility.

families.name: Build apps and services
families.blurb: Frameworks, APIs, databases, mobile and language know-how for writing the thing.

families.name: Test and quality
families.blurb: Tests, reviews and checks that catch problems before users do.

families.name: Security
families.blurb: Find and fix vulnerabilities, harden code, test like an attacker.

families.name: Ship and run
families.blurb: Containers, pipelines, releases, networks and keeping things running.

families.name: Prompts and agents
families.blurb: Work with AI agents: prompting, workflows, memory, evals, skills and tokens.

families.name: Models and gateways
families.blurb: Route between models, use free tiers and local ones, find the right API.

families.name: Run a project (GSD)
families.blurb: Get Shit Done: phases, milestones, plans, reviews and shipping as one workflow.

families.name: Research and docs
families.blurb: Understand a topic or a codebase, then write it down well.

families.name: 3D and creative
families.blurb: Blender scenes, 3D assets, video, writing and marketing content.

families.name: Business and automation
families.blurb: Billing, investors, careers, industries, web3 and n8n automations.
